I submitted an experimental research paper to the Elsevier journal Energy, and its status changed to "Required Reviews Completed" just 20 days after submission.

Is it common for reviewers to complete their reports this quickly? I'm worried that such a short review time might mean the reviewers only had time to recommend rejection rather than provide detailed feedback or suggest revisions.

An undergraduate student submitted an article to an IOP journal, European Journal of Physics, for review. The review verdict was negative, but some part of the verbiage leaves some scope for interpretation.

Relevant excerpts from the Editorial Team's email, are as under:

The Editorial Board has decided this manuscript is not suitable for publication in its current form. Because your Paper needs significant work, it has been rejected and you won’t be able to revise it within this submission process. However, if you choose to rewrite it following the guidance in the report(s), it may be suitable for resubmission and will be sent for further peer review. If you choose to rewrite your Paper, we will treat the rewritten manuscript as a new submission and supply a new reference number.

But another relevant excerpt from the same email reads:

Please ensure that you resubmit your rewritten manuscript within the next 6 months. If you need more time to revise your manuscript, please contact us to arrange an extension.

If one tracks the original manuscript using IOP Article Tracking, it does not show this article in any running workflow. Rather one gets a page:

Unfortunately your submission isn’t suitable for publication, as the reviewers have asked for substantial changes. However you are welcome to resubmit your manuscript if you rewrite the article as explained in the reviewer reports.

Now, 6 months is a fairly wide time-window, and can accommodate one/two review cycles in another journal as well. Since the manuscript is not actively under review currently in this journal, is it an ethical violation if the student submits the revised article to another competing journal, and resubmits here (within 6 months) only if the revised article is also rejected in that second journal? Also, does this first journal have to be informed regarding the submission in the second journal, since the article does not sit in their workflow?
